name: com.battery-snap/batterysnap
title: BatterySnap
description: Real-world Android battery stats from BatterySnap users: device, model and fleet rankings.

tools.name: brands
tools.description:
List the phone brands BatterySnap has battery statistics for, most devices first, with each brand's number
of models and of devices (50 brands unless `limit` says otherwise; `offset` pages).

Each entry also gives the largest single-model device count within the brand (`max_devices_per_model`);
`model_count` counts the models with a known marketing name. Each entry also includes a `url` to the public BatterySnap web page for the brand
(e.g. https://www.battery-snap.com/brands/samsung).
Pass `min_device_count` / `max_device_count` and `min_model_count` / `max_model_count`
to filter brands by recorded-device and distinct-model counts.
Pass `sort` to order otherwise, e.g. sort=[{"by": "brand"}] for A to Z.
Pass `fields` to keep only specific attributes in each entry.
Prefer `search` when resolving one brand by name.

min_device_count.description: Drop entries with fewer than this many recorded devices. Defaults to 1 (keep all).

max_device_count.description: Drop entries with more than this many recorded devices. Use to skip very common entries. Omit for no upper bound.

min_model_count.description: Drop brands with fewer than this many distinct models. Defaults to 0 (keep all).

max_model_count.description: Drop brands with more than this many distinct models. Omit for no upper bound.

order.description: 'asc' (smallest / A first) or 'desc' (largest / Z first). When omitted: 'desc' for counts and other numbers, 'asc' for names.

sort.description: Sort keys, applied in list order: each next key only orders entries the keys before it tie, e.g. [{"by": "device_count"}] = most devices first, [{"by": "model_count", "order": "desc"}, {"by": "device_count"}]. Missing values go last. Sorting runs before `limit` / `offset`, so [{"by": "device_count"}] with limit=10 is the 10 with the most devices. Omit for most devices first; brand always breaks the ties left.

limit.description: Return at most this many entries (50 when omitted). Page with `offset`, or pass a larger limit for more.

offset.description: Skip this many entries before returning results — use with `limit` to page through a long list. Defaults to 0.

fields.description: Attributes to keep in each returned entry, to shrink the response. Omit (or pass an empty list) for all of them.

tools.name: models
tools.description:
List the phone models BatterySnap has battery statistics for (of one `brand`, several `brands` or all),
most devices first, with each model's number of devices, average battery temperature in Celsius and Android
SDK range (50 models unless `limit` says otherwise; `offset` pages).

Each entry is grouped by the resolved street name (e.g. 'Galaxy S23'), which may cover
several raw Android Build.MODEL identifiers (carrier variants, regional SKUs, …). For
URL building, every entry also exposes:
  * `raw_model_code`: a representative raw Build.MODEL identifier (the lexicographically
    smallest one among devices grouped under this street name), or null if no device
    reported a non-empty model code.
  * `url`: the public BatterySnap web page for the model, e.g.
    https://www.battery-snap.com/brands/samsung/models/SM-S911B. Built from `brand` + `raw_model_code`; null when either is null;
    `raw_model_code` is null. The page lists all devices reporting that exact raw model.

Pass `min_device_count` / `max_device_count` to filter models by how many devices were recorded.
Pass `sort` to order by another value (temperature, API levels) or by name, e.g. sort=[{"by": "model"}].
For battery life or charging rankings, use `top_models` instead.
Pass `fields` to keep only specific attributes in each entry
(typically fields=['brand', 'model', 'device_count', 'url']).

brand.description: One lowercase brand identifier (e.g. 'samsung'), as in the other tools. Use `brands` for several.

brands.description: Several lowercase brand identifiers (e.g. ['samsung', 'xiaomi']) to fetch models for. Matched case-insensitively. Omit `brand` and `brands` to list models across all brands.

min_device_count.description: Drop entries with fewer than this many recorded devices. Defaults to 1 (keep all).

max_device_count.description: Drop entries with more than this many recorded devices. Use to skip very common entries. Omit for no upper bound.

order.description: 'asc' (smallest / A first) or 'desc' (largest / Z first). When omitted: 'desc' for counts and other numbers, 'asc' for names.

sort.description: Sort keys, applied in list order: each next key only orders entries the keys before it tie, e.g. [{"by": "device_count"}] = most devices first, [{"by": "temperature_c", "order": "desc"}, {"by": "device_count"}]. Missing values go last. Sorting runs before `limit` / `offset`, so [{"by": "device_count"}] with limit=10 is the 10 with the most devices. Omit for most devices first; brand then model always breaks the ties left.

limit.description: Return at most this many models, after filtering and sorting (50 when omitted).

offset.description: Skip this many entries before returning results — use with `limit` to page through a long list. Defaults to 0.

fields.description: Attributes to keep in each returned entry, to shrink the response. Omit (or pass an empty list) for all of them.

tools.name: devices
tools.description:
Return the list of individual physical devices matching one or more (brand, model) pairs
for which we have battery statistics. Each entry in the returned list describes ONE specific
device (identified by its own `device_uid`) and the metrics on that entry are aggregates
computed only from THAT device's own snapshot history — they are not aggregated across
devices. Two devices of the same brand and model will appear as two separate entries with
their own independent metrics.

Each entry has: brand (lowercase brand, e.g. 'samsung'), device_uid (this device's id, for device_summary / device_ranking), url (public page with the device's battery history), model (model name, e.g. 'Galaxy S23'), raw_model (Build.MODEL code, e.g. 'SM-S911B'), snapshot_count (number of battery readings, more = more reliable), battery_level_pct (average charge level, %), temperature_c (average battery temperature, C), min_temperature_c (coldest battery temperature, C), max_temperature_c (hottest battery temperature, C), awake_ratio (fraction of time awake / screen-on, 0..1), discharge_hours (discharge time / battery life, hours per 100%, higher = longer), ac_charge_hours (AC charge time, hours per 100%, lower = faster), usb_charge_hours (USB charge time, hours per 100%, lower = faster), wireless_charge_hours (wireless charge time, hours per 100%, lower = faster), android_api_level (Android SDK level, e.g. 34 = Android 14).

Each pair's model is matched case-insensitively against either the resolved street name
(e.g. 'Galaxy S23') or the raw Android model identifier (e.g. 'SM-S911B').
Pass `fields` to keep only specific attributes per device and avoid bloated responses.

pairs.description: One or more {brand, model} pairs to look up. Each pair fetches devices matching that brand and model.

brand.description: Lowercase Android device brand identifier (e.g. 'samsung', 'xiaomi'), matched case-insensitively against the device's brand.

model.description: Model name matched case-insensitively against either the resolved street name (e.g. 'Galaxy S23') or the raw Android model identifier (e.g. 'SM-S911B').

fields.description: Attributes to keep in each returned entry, to shrink the response. Omit (or pass an empty list) for all of them. Names: brand (lowercase brand, e.g. 'samsung'), device_uid (this device's id, for device_summary / device_ranking), url (public page with the device's battery history), model (model name, e.g. 'Galaxy S23'), raw_model (Build.MODEL code, e.g. 'SM-S911B'), snapshot_count (number of battery readings, more = more reliable), battery_level_pct (average charge level, %), temperature_c (average battery temperature, C), min_temperature_c (coldest battery temperature, C), max_temperature_c (hottest battery temperature, C), awake_ratio (fraction of time awake / screen-on, 0..1), discharge_hours (discharge time / battery life, hours per 100%, higher = longer), ac_charge_hours (AC charge time, hours per 100%, lower = faster), usb_charge_hours (USB charge time, hours per 100%, lower = faster), wireless_charge_hours (wireless charge time, hours per 100%, lower = faster), android_api_level (Android SDK level, e.g. 34 = Android 14).

tools.name: device_summary
tools.description:
Return aggregated battery metrics for ONE specific device: average / min / max
temperature, average battery level, mean charge time per power source (AC, USB,
wireless) and mean discharge time over a recent (~2 weeks) and a long (~2 months)
window, plus awake ratio and basic device info. Also includes `url`: the public
BatterySnap web page for this device's interactive battery history
(https://www.battery-snap.com/device_history?device=<uid>). All values are pre-computed
from the device's full snapshot history — no raw timeseries is returned.

device_uid.description: Stable device UUID returned by the `devices` tool.

tools.name: model_summary
tools.description:
Aggregate battery metrics across ALL devices of a given brand+model. Returns
mean / median / p25 / p75 / min / max for: temperature (C), battery level (%),
discharge speed (hours per 100%%), AC / USB / wireless charge speed (hours per
100%%), and awake ratio. Use this to characterize how a model behaves in the
field, or to compare a single device against its model average.

Also includes:
  * `raw_model_code`: representative raw Android Build.MODEL identifier (smallest
    among devices grouped under this street name), or null if none recorded.
  * `url`: public BatterySnap web page for the model
    (https://www.battery-snap.com/brands/<brand>/models/<raw_model_code>); null when
    `raw_model_code` is null.

Pass `country` and / or `continent` to restrict to devices of that region; the
call fails when fewer than 5 devices of the model remain.

model.description: Model name, matched against resolved street name (e.g. 'Galaxy S23') or raw Build.MODEL (e.g. 'SM-S911B').

country.description: Optional ISO 3166 alpha-2 country code (e.g. 'FR', 'IN', 'US'), case-insensitive. Keeps only devices whose time zone belongs to that country. The region comes from the phone's time-zone setting, not GPS / IP.

continent.description: Optional continent. Keeps only devices whose time zone lies there. Combine with `country` for an intersection.

tools.name: fleet_totals
tools.description:
Live fleet-wide counters: total devices, models, snapshots, sessions, the
running snapshot-ingest rate (snapshots/sec) and the timing of the last
insert batch. Use this for one-shot 'how big is the dataset / how fast is it
growing' questions. Unlike `fleet_summary`, no per-device aggregation is
involved — these are raw running counts from the database.

tools.name: fleet_summary
tools.description:
Aggregate battery metrics across the entire fleet, or across one brand when
`brand` is provided, optionally restricted to one `country` / `continent`.
Returns mean / median / p25 / p75 / min / max for the same set of metrics as
`model_summary`. Use this for fleet-wide baselines that a single device or
model can be compared against. A region scope with fewer than 5 devices is
refused; to compare several regions at once use `region_summary`.

brand.description: Optional lowercase brand identifier. If set, aggregates across that brand only; otherwise across the entire fleet.

country.description: Optional ISO 3166 alpha-2 country code (e.g. 'FR', 'IN', 'US'), case-insensitive. Keeps only devices whose time zone belongs to that country. The region comes from the phone's time-zone setting, not GPS / IP.

continent.description: Optional continent. Keeps only devices whose time zone lies there. Combine with `country` for an intersection.

tools.name: region_summary
tools.description:
Compare battery behaviour across regions in one call: one entry per
continent or per country, each with the same mean / median / p25 / p75 /
min / max blocks as `fleet_summary` (temperature, level, discharge and
charge hours, awake ratio). Narrow with `brand` / `model` (e.g. how one
model fares per continent) or with `continent` (e.g. group_by='country'
within 'Africa').

The region is derived from the time zone the phone is set to (not GPS / IP),
so travellers and manual settings blur it. Regions with fewer than 5 devices
are left out and only counted (`suppressed_*`), as are devices whose time
zone names no place (`unlocated_device_count`); check each group's
`device_count` before comparing — small groups are noisy.

model.description: Optional model filter — matches resolved street name or raw Build.MODEL, case-insensitive.

country.description: Optional ISO 3166 alpha-2 country code (e.g. 'FR', 'IN', 'US'), case-insensitive. Keeps only devices whose time zone belongs to that country. The region comes from the phone's time-zone setting, not GPS / IP.

continent.description: Optional continent. Keeps only devices whose time zone lies there. Combine with `country` for an intersection.

tools.name: top_devices_by_uptime
tools.description:
Return the devices with the longest single uptime ever recorded between
reboots (max_elapsed_time). Optionally filter by brand and/or model. Useful
to find which physical phones in the fleet are champions of staying powered
on for weeks/months at a time. Each entry includes a `device_uid` you can
feed into `device_summary` for deeper analysis, and a `url` pointing at the
device's interactive battery history page on https://www.battery-snap.com.

brand.description: Optional lowercase brand filter. When omitted, devices from any brand are ranked together.

model.description: Optional model filter — matches resolved street name or raw Build.MODEL, case-insensitive. When omitted, no model filter applies.

tools.name: top_devices_by_live_uptime
tools.description:
Same as `top_devices_by_uptime`, but restricted to devices that have not
yet rebooted past their recorded maximum — meaning the uptime is currently
still climbing. These are the devices that are 'live' champions right now,
as opposed to historical record-holders. Each entry includes a `url`
pointing at the device's interactive battery history page on
https://www.battery-snap.com.

brand.description: Optional lowercase brand filter. When omitted, devices from any brand are ranked together.

model.description: Optional model filter — matches resolved street name or raw Build.MODEL, case-insensitive. When omitted, no model filter applies.

tools.name: top_devices
tools.description:
Rank INDIVIDUAL devices by any battery metric — the general-purpose
leaderboard. Use it for 'which phones run hottest / last longest / charge
fastest', optionally narrowed to one brand and/or model. Returns at most
`limit` rows, so it answers superlative questions in a single small call
instead of enumerating the fleet. Pair the metric with the right `order`:
hottest = temperature_c + desc, fastest AC charging = ac_charge_hours + asc,
best battery life = discharge_hours + desc. To compare phones the user
names, call `model_summary` for each of them instead.

Ranking is over each device's own lifetime aggregate.
There is no region filter here: regional questions go to the aggregates
(`region_summary`, `top_models`, `fleet_summary`).

metric.description: Which battery metric to rank on. One of: 'temperature_c' (mean battery temperature, C), 'max_temperature_c' / 'min_temperature_c' (hottest / coldest ever seen, C), 'battery_level_pct' (mean charge level, 0-100), 'discharge_hours' (hours to drain a full 100% - HIGHER means longer battery life), 'ac_charge_hours' / 'usb_charge_hours' / 'wireless_charge_hours' (hours to charge a full 100% on that source - LOWER means faster charging), 'awake_ratio' (fraction of time awake / screen-on, 0..1), 'snapshot_count' (how much data the device contributed), 'uptime_hours' (longest single uptime between reboots).

order.description: 'desc' (default) ranks the highest values first, 'asc' the lowest. Pick the direction that matches the question: fastest charging is ac_charge_hours + asc; longest battery life is discharge_hours + desc.

brand.description: Optional lowercase brand filter. When omitted, devices from any brand are ranked together.

model.description: Optional model filter — matches resolved street name or raw Build.MODEL, case-insensitive. When omitted, no model filter applies.

min_snapshots.description: Ignore devices with fewer snapshots than this. Defaults to 100, which filters out barely-sampled devices whose averages are meaningless. Lower it only when a query returns too few rows.

tools.name: top_models
tools.description:
Rank device MODELS by any battery metric, aggregating across every device
of that model. This is the tool for 'which phone model has the best battery
life', 'which models charge fastest', 'which run hottest' — questions that
would otherwise need one `model_summary` call per model. Pair the metric
with the right `order`: hottest = temperature_c + desc, fastest AC charging
= ac_charge_hours + asc, best battery life = discharge_hours + desc. To
compare phones the user names, call `model_summary` for each of them instead.

Ordering is by the per-model MEDIAN of the metric (outlier-resistant); the
mean is returned alongside. Use `brand` to rank within one manufacturer and
`min_devices` to require a minimum sample size. `country` / `continent` rank
the models as they behave in one region (e.g. heat in hot climates).

metric.description: Which battery metric to rank on. One of: 'temperature_c' (mean battery temperature, C), 'max_temperature_c' / 'min_temperature_c' (hottest / coldest ever seen, C), 'battery_level_pct' (mean charge level, 0-100), 'discharge_hours' (hours to drain a full 100% - HIGHER means longer battery life), 'ac_charge_hours' / 'usb_charge_hours' / 'wireless_charge_hours' (hours to charge a full 100% on that source - LOWER means faster charging), 'awake_ratio' (fraction of time awake / screen-on, 0..1), 'snapshot_count' (how much data the device contributed), 'uptime_hours' (longest single uptime between reboots).

order.description: 'desc' (default) ranks the highest values first, 'asc' the lowest. Pick the direction that matches the question: fastest charging is ac_charge_hours + asc; longest battery life is discharge_hours + desc.

brand.description: Optional lowercase brand filter. When omitted, devices from any brand are ranked together.

min_devices.description: Ignore models backed by fewer devices than this. Defaults to 3 so a single outlier phone cannot win a ranking. Raise it for more robust comparisons. Raised to at least 5 when a region filter is set.

country.description: Optional ISO 3166 alpha-2 country code (e.g. 'FR', 'IN', 'US'), case-insensitive. Keeps only devices whose time zone belongs to that country. The region comes from the phone's time-zone setting, not GPS / IP.

continent.description: Optional continent. Keeps only devices whose time zone lies there. Combine with `country` for an intersection.

tools.name: device_ranking
tools.description:
Answer 'is MY phone normal?' — rank one device's metric against other
devices of the same model AND against the whole fleet, in one call. Returns
the device's value, its 1-based rank, its percentile, and the cohort
median / mean / min / max for both cohorts.

Prefer this over fetching `device_summary` + `model_summary` and comparing
by hand: it is a single call and gives the percentile directly. The model
cohort is the meaningful one for 'is this device degraded'; the fleet cohort
puts the model itself in context.

device_uid.description: Stable device UUID returned by `devices`, `top_devices` or the share flow.

metric.description: Which battery metric to rank on. One of: 'temperature_c' (mean battery temperature, C), 'max_temperature_c' / 'min_temperature_c' (hottest / coldest ever seen, C), 'battery_level_pct' (mean charge level, 0-100), 'discharge_hours' (hours to drain a full 100% - HIGHER means longer battery life), 'ac_charge_hours' / 'usb_charge_hours' / 'wireless_charge_hours' (hours to charge a full 100% on that source - LOWER means faster charging), 'awake_ratio' (fraction of time awake / screen-on, 0..1), 'snapshot_count' (how much data the device contributed), 'uptime_hours' (longest single uptime between reboots).

tools.name: search
tools.description:
Resolve free-form user text into the canonical brand / model identifiers
the other tools expect. Meant for phones named in free text: the other tools
match brands and models exactly, so a guessed spelling returns an empty
list.

Matching is substring-based and case-insensitive over brand, resolved model
name and raw Build.MODEL, ranked by exact match then popularity.

query.description: Free text: a brand ('samsug'), a model name ('pixel 8'), a raw Build.MODEL code ('SM-S911B'), or both ('samsung galaxy s23').

limit.description: Maximum brand hits and model hits to return (each list is capped separately).
